newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end Tokyo firmer, but surrender most gains.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end Tokyo firmer, but surrender most gains.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended firmer on Tuesday, but surrendered most of its gains built during the day due to dealers' profit-taking towards the close, traders said.
The rally in the early afternoon was led by cash bond purchases by regional financial institutions and some city banks' portfolio accounts.

Some said the bond rally was also helped by a news agency report that the BOJ's quarterly corporate survey, known as the "tankan", was likely to show only a limited improvement in sentiment at small- and medium-sized firms.
The report concluded that the results of the tankan would prompt the BOJ to maintain its easy monetary policy.

Overseas speculators also joined the JGB rally, expanding their long positions in the December contract, but they closed those fresh long positions by the futures market close, accentuating the December's late afternoon losses.
The December ended at 125.47, up from Monday's 125.32. It hit a high of 126.12 in the early afternoon.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB stood at 2.545 percent at 0646 GMT, down from 2.560 percent on Monday.
Some regional financial institutions, expecting a lower coupon rate on new 10-year JGBs to be offered next week, placed bids on the current 10-year JGBs with a 2.9 percent coupon, they said.
The market is waiting for Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita's news conference on Wednesday, ahead of the BOJ's quarterly tankan corporate survey on November 27.
The key December is likely to give up its benchmark status after the results of the tankan, traders said.
Open interest in the December was still at a large 17.1299 trillion yen.
